title: Temple of Edfu
visualBrief: Specific Edfu exterior: twin battered pylons and open gateway, open forecourt and peristyle, raised column-fronted roofed hall, independently mapped rear roof ranges and enclosing passage wall. The separate southern mapped colonnaded building retains all fourteen column controls and rear wall controls. No generic archaeological-park mass substitutes for the temple.

sourceFacts.horizontalBasis: Q613037 identifies Temple of Edfu. Standard PMTiles building52776572243683 supplies its eight-point perimeter and open inner court; five independent roof-range controls and the southern building with fifteen parts retain their own positions. The593-by258m archaeological-site boundary is not the temple footprint. Raw+X east/+Z south and heading0 preserve the signed south-facing pylon front,2.08 degrees west of south.
sourceFacts.architecturalHeights: Retained nominal facts give137m length,79m width and36m pylon height. Mapped wall envelope is about73by143m; tower taper, cornices, staff recesses and open portal follow one ordinary frontal photograph. Court columns, roof heights, simplified falcons and southern building elevation are visualization estimates; no exact relief or inscription inventory.

Reviewed approximate full-site fit on the unchanged161-square/6m standard DEM. Cross-axis medians set a graded visualization floor; both occupied compounds retain complete floors in every level. Local ground openings and perimeter joins remain bounded to those compounds. Loading replaces22 mapped temple/column records and preserves26 independent buildings in the960m tile exactly;27 independent records are preserved across the larger extract. No water is present in this local extract. Failure retains all48 native tile buildings and original ground; eviction restores ground and frees all geometry. A synthetic64m partial tile verifies clipping and lifecycle only. It exposes the existing terrain-excavation sky-sliver limitation at temporary clipped boundaries; full-site contact does not approve those temporary edges.
